description: Palimpsest. Lower text: Aquila’s Greek translation of II Kings 23:11–27, copied in the 6th century. Uses paleo-Hebrew characters for the tetragrammaton. This word was apparently pronounced kurios, ‘lord’ (a translation of the Hebrew adonay): on folio 2b, col. a, line 15, at the end of 2 Kings 23:24, the scribe ran out of room to write the tetragrammaton and instead wrote κυ (an abbreviation of κύριος). Upper text: piyyuṭim of the liturgical poet Yannai, copied 9th–11th century CE, Qerovot on four sedarim in Leviticus (13:29; 14:1; 21:1; 22:13). These form a complete quire together with T-S 12.182 and T-S 12.184 (PGPID 38688). (Information from CUDL)
